text:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: Service=redis-primary | Trigger=clients_maxed | Severity=P1 | Incident=PD-8921 | Runbook: https://runbook.internal/runbooks/redis-maxclients
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert fired -> PD-8921. Paging on-call.
alex: ack PD-8921 - I'm on it. @jamie @maria can you confirm customer impact and any recent deploys?
jamie: seeing a spike in 5xx from /embeddings and /cache-warm, ~10% errors over last 5m. p99 redis op latency ~450ms. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/redis/prod-cluster
alex: quick check via redis-cli: ```
# Clients
connected_clients:9998
blocked_clients:12
maxclients:10000
```
we're at ~99.98% of maxclients on primary cluster.
maria: wow. any long-lived connections?
alex: looks correlated with the batch-ingest v2 rollout around 03:50UTC — the service opened many persistent connections without client pooling.
jamie: propose mitigation steps: 1) throttle batch-ingest traffic at edge 2) spin up 2 extra read replicas for cache offload 3) temporarily increase maxclients on primaries 4) identify and kill stray long-lived clients 5) notify customers/status page
alex: applying step 1 now: adding a rate-limit rule in envoy to throttle batch-ingest to 30rps `kubectl apply -f -` (pushing patch).
incident-bot: Automation: runbook step 'throttle-batch-ingest' started by alex.
alex: throttle applied, traffic to /batch-ingest dropped ~70% (confirmed on edge logs). :thumbsup:
jamie: starting replica spin-up: `./scripts/redis-scale-replica.sh --count 2` — launching as read-only cache nodes.
maria: caution on replication lag; only use replicas for non-critical cache reads.
alex: coordinating infra to bump maxclients on nodes one at a time. Planned command (dry-run): ```bash
for host in redis-01 redis-02 redis-03; do 
  ssh $host "sudo sed -i 's/^maxclients .*/maxclients 20000/' /etc/redis/redis.conf && sudo systemctl restart redis"
done
```
will restart one host at a time, watching customer impact.
infra-team: acknowledged, restarting redis-02 now. We'll watch for failover churn.
pagerduty-bot: PD-8921 acknowledged by alex.
incident-bot: PD-8921 escalation paused (acknowledged).
alex: restart of redis-02 completed; after restart that host reported connected_clients ~3200, cluster redistributed load, total client count dropped ~40%. saw a couple of transient errors during restart but overall stability improved.
maria: customer impact summary: 12 customers showing elevated errors, biggest ones are enterprise customers doing bulk embedding jobs. Error budget hit ~8% in the last 30m for embedding pipeline. Cust-ops ticket created: COPS-431.
jamie: drafted status page update: "Partial degradation of caching layer affecting read-heavy endpoints; engineers are mitigating. Some customers may see increased latency or 5xx errors for embeddings and cache-warm endpoints." Please review before posting.
alex: posting update to status page now.
alex: handing on-call to night shift @maria in 20m — I'll leave runbook notes and a quick remediation checklist.
maria: taking over. Running a connection audit: `./sre/conn-audit.py --service redis-primary --stale-seconds 60` to find long-lived clients.
alex: notes for post-incident: - root cause: batch-ingest v2 opened many non-pooled persistent connections -> exhausted maxclients threshold - short-term: throttle, bump maxclients, add read-only replicas - long-term: enforce pooled client library usage, add connection-count per-deployment alert, improve rollout gating for connection-heavy releases.
maria: ack. I'll follow up with a full incident write-up and timeline. Will close PD once errors <1% for 30m and replicas stable.
pagerduty-bot: PD-8921 status: acknowledged; responders: alex, maria, jamie; escalation path paused.
